$comment: The mutation matrix: break a valid payload in a known way and prove that validation fails.
Declared here once, in data, and applied by BOTH test suites - pytest with jsonschema, vitest
with Ajv, against the same hand-written schema/gufe-viz.schema.json.
This matrix is the load-bearing half of schema-first. Correctness comes from testing.
Each entry takes a valid payload from examples/, applies one JSON-Pointer operation, and states
what must happen. `types` restricts an entry to payloads of those types; absent means all of them.
`expect` is 'invalid' (both validators must reject it) or 'valid' (both must accept it - the
render-degraded rows, which are just as important to pin down: schema validity is not chemical
validity, and the views are what handle the difference).
`pointerContains` is asserted against the reported error location, so a rejection for the wrong
reason does not pass as a rejection. An empty string means the error is reported at the root,
which is where both validators report a missing required property.

mutations.why: Without `type` there is nothing to say what the payload is.
A type nobody declared must be refused, not guessed at. The union is closed.
additionalProperties:false - a misspelled key must fail loudly rather than render blank.
sdf is required on a small molecule: there is nothing to draw without it.
Same, for each of the three types that carry a PDB.
Same, for a network's ligands.
Every payload stands for a GufeTokenizable and carries its key. Without one it cannot be put in a registry, cannot be referred to, and cannot be identified when it fails to draw.
minLength:1 - an empty key is a builder that read `.key` off something that does not have one, and it would silently collide with every other empty key in the registry.
A network's nodes are gufe keys, so without a registry there is nothing for them to resolve to and no ligand to draw.
A string where a number belongs is the classic payload-builder typo, and the error must name the field.
Same, for a required string field.
minLength:1 - an empty sdf is a builder that produced nothing, and is worth catching at the contract rather than as a blank picture.
A network's edges are a list; an object there is the shape a hand-written payload gets wrong.

The shape this field used to have. An object keyed by a stringified A index carries the same information, but it makes the indices strings on the wire and cannot state that every A index has a B index - which is why it was replaced, and why it must not quietly validate now.
The constraint the list shape exists to buy: an A index with nothing to map it to is not a correspondence, and the schema now says so rather than leaving it to a builder.
Both sides are atom indices, so a negative number cannot be one.
A pair is exactly two indices. An extra key is a hand-written payload inventing a field the views will never read.
Nodes are gufe keys into the registry, not inlined objects. Putting the object back where the key belongs is the shape the old schema had, and it must not quietly validate under the new one.
The same rule inside a chemical system: `components` maps a label to a gufe key, and the component itself lives in the registry.

mutations.$comment: The per-type exclusivity rows. Each is stated twice, once against a standalone component and once against the same component sitting in a registry, because the single ComponentViz union claims those are the same object.
mutations.why: A small molecule carries an sdf and cannot also carry a pdb. Each component type declares only its own structure field, so the other one is an unknown key.
A solvent is a specification, not a structure: there is no sdf field to fill.

The same rule from the other side, for all three PDB-carrying types: each carries a pdb and only a pdb. Applying it to the two subclasses matters because they are the types most likely to acquire an extra field by being confused with their parent.

The discriminator is what a view dispatches on, and the three PDB types are a subclass chain in gufe. A payload built from a ProteinMembraneComponent that says it is a plain ProteinComponentViz is still schema-valid - the shapes are identical - so this row pins that the schema cannot catch it and a builder-ordering test must.

mutations.$comment: Registry entries are sorted by (type, gufe-key), so entry 0 of a chemical system's registry and of a ligand network's registry is a small molecule in both. The rows below that need a specific type say so with `types`; the rest hold for any entry at all.
mutations.why: The same exclusivity, one level down: a component in a registry is validated as itself, so the rule holds there identically. This is what replaces the old 'nested component' rows - components are reached through the registry now, not inlined.
Same, from the other side: a chemical system's registry holds its solvent at entry 1, and a solvent is a specification rather than a structure.
Each component subschema declares only its own fields, so a solvent setting on a small molecule is an unknown key rather than a permitted null.
A registry entry with no gufe key can never be found: the key is the only way anything refers to it.
The registry union is closed. An unrecognized gufe class is carried as an UnknownComponentViz by the builder, not smuggled through under its own name.

mutations.$comment: Rows that must still be ACCEPTED. Schema validity is not chemical validity, and pinning down what the contract deliberately does not check matters as much as pinning down what it does.
mutations.why: The contract does not parse chemistry, so this passes validation and is caught by the view instead - an error panel, not a crash.
mutations.value:
not an SDF at all

mutations.why: JSON Schema cannot express 'componentA names a node that exists', so this validates and the view drops the edge with a banner. A Python test covers the referential integrity that the schema cannot.
The other half of the same gap: JSON Schema cannot express 'this key names a registry entry'. The view drops the node with a banner, and a Python test holds the builders to never emitting one.
An unreferenced entry is waste, not corruption - a builder that registered something and then did not use it. The contract does not forbid it and the views ignore it.
Annotations are deliberately open: every mapper picks its own keys, and a new one must not break an older reader.
A chemical system with no components is odd but not malformed, and the view says so rather than the validator.
